assumptions: The supplied gateway snapshot matches the deployed code closely enough for static capability claims; live probes are still required.
The candidate fix will be minted unattached and tested with synthetic, non-production-impacting data.
A true latest-slot claim requires access to the complete same-day inventory, not merely reversal of an already truncated list.
unique_catches: The diagnosis phrase 'availability call runs and never renders' conflates two layers: both supplied incident calls actually completed quickly with HTTP 409; the missing evidence is the 409 body and Bland route/render trace.
The same n_miss_unread prompt authorizes both observed behaviors, so divergent copy does not prove two different nodes or builds.

Gateway before/time-bound support is present, but latest-first ordering is a separate absent capability; before alone cannot express 'last slot of day' without a known closing anchor and complete inventory.
The current validator protects the 20 shared prompt paragraphs rather than asserting filler absence, so a filler-strip patch needs a deliberate validator rule change and redproof.
risks_or_failure_modes: Removing filler can turn filler-plus-silence into silence without repairing routing or response rendering.
Reversing slots[0:2] pathway-side can falsely label a truncated subset as the day's latest slots.
A generic descending change can regress ordinary earliest/soonest requests unless ordering is explicitly scoped.
A 409 or timeout can still strand the conversation unless its response mapping has an explicit patient-visible failure route.
Edge-label text is not proof that Bland selects the edge for actual time-preference utterances.
Harness traffic shares gateway capacity with the live line; execute before opening and avoid concurrent live load.
proof_slots: Run `python3 checks/check_v91_graph.py --base pathway-v86.json --draft <CANDIDATE_JSON> --v88-ref pathway-v90.json --classification <CANDIDATE_CLASSIFICATION_JSON>`; require clean exit 0 and observed nonzero exits for filler, routing, before/ordering, mapping, and regression mutations.

Run `python3 checks/phase_run.py <CANDIDATE_VERSION> phase1` with the added exact script `hi -> Friday 08/14 -> What's the last time of the day I can come in?`; require one response, an offer node rather than n_miss_unread, no filler/referral, and returned final-two inventory slots latest first.

Run `python3 checks/phase_run.py <CANDIDATE_VERSION> phase1` with `hi -> Friday 08/14 before 2pm` and `hi -> Friday 08/14 after 3pm`; assert spoken slots are same-turn inventory members and satisfy the strict upper/lower bounds.

Run a read-only `curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$GW_URL/availability" ... | jq .` baseline and candidate-latest A/B on one populated day; require candidate choices equal the baseline's final two chronological slots, latest first.
Run the same curl shape with `before:02:00 pm`; require HTTP 200 and every returned slot strictly before 14:00, proving deployed before-bound support.

Replay `hi -> Friday 08/14 -> last time of the day -> Hello?` through the unattached harness; require one attributable availability call, no duplicate filler, explicit offer or safe failure, and patient-visible latency <=15 seconds.
